audit_source:
import ErdosProblems.Erdos79

open scoped SimpleGraph

/- Existing public proof evidence. This audit does not replace the upstream proof. -/
namespace JSP096Audit

theorem uniform_bound_iff (F : Erdos79.GraphCode) :
    Erdos79.RamseySizeLinear F ↔
      ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ H : Erdos79.GraphCode,
        (∀ v, ¬ H.graph.IsIsolated v) →
        Erdos79.graphRamseyNumber F H ≤ C * Nat.card H.graph.edgeSet :=
  Erdos79.RamseySizeLinear.iff_graphRamseyNumber_le

/- This spells out the original infinitude question in terms of least Ramsey
numbers, ordinary graph copies, and ordinary graph isomorphisms. -/
theorem original_infinitude :
    ∃ f : ℕ → Erdos79.GraphCode,
      (∀ n,
        (¬ ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ H : Erdos79.GraphCode,
          (∀ v, ¬ H.graph.IsIsolated v) →
          Erdos79.graphRamseyNumber (f n) H ≤ C * Nat.card H.graph.edgeSet) ∧
        (∀ F : Erdos79.GraphCode,
          F.graph ⊑ (f n).graph →
          ¬ Nonempty (F.graph ≃g (f n).graph) →
          ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ H : Erdos79.GraphCode,
            (∀ v, ¬ H.graph.IsIsolated v) →
            Erdos79.graphRamseyNumber F H ≤ C * Nat.card H.graph.edgeSet)) ∧
      Pairwise fun i j ↦ ¬ Nonempty ((f i).graph ≃g (f j).graph) := by
  obtain ⟨f, hminimal, hnoniso⟩ := Erdos79.erdos_79
  refine ⟨f, ?_, hnoniso⟩
  intro n
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (hminimal n).1 ((uniform_bound_iff (f n)).mpr h)
  · intro F hcopy hnonisoF
    exact (uniform_bound_iff F).mp ((hminimal n).2 F ⟨hcopy, hnonisoF⟩)

#print axioms Erdos79.erdos_79
#print axioms Erdos79.infinitudeInputs
#print axioms Erdos79.ramseySizeLinear_of_isAcyclic
#print axioms Erdos79.not_ramseySizeLinear_of_five_mul_vertexCount_lt_edgeCount
#print axioms Erdos79.exists_dense_highGirth
#print axioms uniform_bound_iff
#print axioms original_infinitude

end JSP096Audit

scope_review_markdown:
# Source-scope review: JSP-000096 / Erdős 79

Source-level verdict: the final theorem covers the original infinitude question. It does not classify all minimal obstructions or exhibit an explicit new obstruction. Runtime verification completed on 2026-09-16: nine compilations and eight explicit leaf replays exited 0; all seven named axiom reports contain only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Exact receipts and logs are embedded in public-evidence.json.

## Original question and catalogue wording

The fixed [JSP catalogue entry](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/f4e7173d89dfe91022a185427d63452c8ffbf6ae/problems/catalog-0001-0100.md#jsp-000096) links the same historical problem and Wigderson paper as [Erdős 79](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/79). The original question asks for infinitely many finite graphs that fail Ramsey size linearity while all their proper subgraphs satisfy it. The published answer is affirmative. [Yuval Wigderson's paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05931) has the title *Infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey size-linear graphs*.

The catalogue instead says “Characterize these obstructions” and omits “non-” from its linked paper title. Those are broader/inaccurate metadata, not extra conclusions proved by the source. [The paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05931v2) leaves an explicit example apart from K4 open. Registration should identify the original infinitude result and request clarification of the catalogue wording; it must not claim a full classification.

## Definition audit

The pinned [Core module](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos79/Core.lean) uses `GraphCode = Σ n : ℕ, SimpleGraph (Fin n)`. Every finite simple graph has such a presentation by a bijection of its vertex set with `Fin n`. `IsContained` is ordinary, non-induced graph-copy containment. `Isomorphic` is nonemptiness of an actual graph isomorphism, which also reflects adjacency.

`RamseyAt F H N` universally quantifies over every simple graph C on `Fin N`, requiring a copy of F in C or a copy of H in its complement. This is exactly a red/blue coloring of the complete graph, with red edges C and blue edges its complement. It is not an induced Ramsey condition. `graphRamseyNumber` is `Nat.find` of a proved finite existence theorem, not an infimum with an empty-set default. `ramseyAt_iff_graphRamseyNumber_le` proves its least-number semantics.

`NoIsolated H` quantifies over every vertex and excludes isolated vertices. The empty graph satisfies it vacuously; a nonempty edgeless graph does not. For empty H, a blue empty copy exists already at N = 0, so requiring `R(F,H) ≤ C * e(H)` when e(H) = 0 adds no unwanted restriction.

`RamseySizeLinear F` is `∃ C : ℕ, ∀ H, NoIsolated H → RamseyAt F H (C * H.edgeCount)`. The quantifier order makes one constant depend on F and work for every H. The source proves equivalence to `R(F,H) ≤ C * e(H)`. Allowing a real positive constant instead gives the same property: increase it to a positive natural ceiling; conversely increase a natural witness to a positive real witness. This arithmetic observation is a mathematical scope identification, not an additional compiled real-constant equivalence. `GraphCode.edgeCount` is the number of unordered undirected edges, via `Nat.card edgeSet`.

The pinned [Minimal module](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos79/Minimal.lean) defines a proper subgraph by ordinary containment and failure of isomorphism. For finite graphs, an embedding with equal vertex and edge counts is an isomorphism, as proved there. Thus proper containment strictly decreases the sum of these counts. This includes edge deletion and vertex deletion; it is not merely induced-subgraph minimality. The extraction of a minimal bad subgraph uses `Nat.sInf_mem` with an explicit witness that the set of bad-subgraph sizes is nonempty (the original bad graph itself). There is no empty-infimum loophole.

## Closed inputs and final theorem

The final [Erdos79 module](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos79.lean) supplies all three inputs to its infinitude argument from imported proofs:

1. Every finite forest is Ramsey size linear (`ramseySizeLinear_of_isAcyclic`), including disconnected forests and the empty forest.
2. If `5 * vertexCount < edgeCount`, the graph is not Ramsey size linear (`not_ramseySizeLinear_of_five_mul_vertexCount_lt_edgeCount`). The first-moment construction uses red edge probability 1/k, ambient order k^5 and blue target K_(k^2); the witness is chosen after the candidate constant. This weaker density criterion than the paper's suffices here.
3. For every natural girth bound g there is a graph with extended girth at least g and `6 * vertexCount < edgeCount` (`exists_dense_highGirth`). A finite random construction and removal of short cycles prove this input. The stronger density guarantees the preceding strict 5-times criterion. `egirth : ℕ∞` treats acyclic graphs by infinite girth consistently; strict positive density prevents an empty witness from doing the work.

Although the reusable `exists_pairwise_nonisomorphic_sequence` accepts an `InfinitudeInputs` hypothesis, `Erdos79.erdos_79` has no such hypothesis: `Erdos79.infinitudeInputs` constructs it from these proved endpoints. The minimization/avoidance argument selects a new minimal obstruction outside each finite family and returns an ℕ-indexed sequence whose members are pairwise nonisomorphic. This establishes infinitely many isomorphism classes, not just infinitely many vertex relabelings.

The compiled local `JSP096Audit.original_infinitude` expands minimality, no-isolated-vertex bounds and pairwise nonisomorphism in a typed statement. It deliberately claims no enumeration algorithm or complete obstruction list. It compiled and its module received an explicit single-target replay.

## Attribution, permissions and verification limits

The upstream header says “Yufei Wigderson”; the primary paper identifies **Yuval Wigderson**. Our metadata uses the paper's name and records the header discrepancy without editing the upstream source. The formal-author notice lists **Codex** and **GPT-5.6 Sol**. Those notices are preserved as attribution records, not as a claim that we authored the formalization.

The pinned `src/latest/LICENSE` says only that some external files use Apache 2.0; it does not identify Erdos79 or Util.Ramsey as covered. No clear license grant for redistributing this proof source is asserted. The public package contains immutable upstream links, hashes, our audit and review, and sanitized logs; the original proof source is not copied into it.

The eight source modules (2624 lines) have no flagged tokens in the comment/string-masked lexical scan. This is not an axiom trace. The completed verification compiled all eight modules and the typed audit into an isolated build directory. It explicitly replayed the seven upstream leaf modules and the typed audit: **nine compilations, eight checker targets**. The main `ErdosProblems.Erdos79` wrapper is compile-only because leanchecker uses module-prefix selection and would also select the child modules. Its full original statement is reexported by the typed audit, which also prints the main theorem's axioms; this is not an explicit replay of the main wrapper. Imported modules remain trusted by each replay, including the compile-only main wrapper when Audit is replayed; Mathlib and standard-library artifacts are prebuilt. The checker shares Lean's implementation; no independent checker implementation, official verifier, prize eligibility, or original/first formalization is claimed.
